## Core Overview
- Course Code: CSC301
- Course Title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
- Credit Hours: 3(3,0)
- Prerequisite: CSC211-Data Structures and Algorithms
- Purpose: Provide mastery over the principles and techniques used in designing efficient algorithms and analyzing their computational complexity.
- Fundamental Themes: Correctness proofs, asymptotic growth, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, greedy strategies, graph algorithms, and intractability (NP-completeness).

## Key Concepts & Theorems/Formulas
- Asymptotic Notations: Big-O, Omega, and Theta notations used to describe the limiting behavior of functions.
- Recurrence Relations: Mathematical equations used in recursive algorithms, solved via Substitution Method, Recurrence Tree Method, and the Master Theorem.
- Sorting & Order Statistics: Comparison-based sorts (Merge Sort, QuickSort, HeapSort running in O(n log n)) and linear-time sorts (Counting Sort, Radix Sort).
- Dynamic Programming: Optimization technique breaking problems into overlapping subproblems (e.g., Matrix Chain Multiplication, 0/1 Knapsack, Longest Common Subsequence, Edit Distance).
- Greedy Algorithms: Making locally optimal choices hoping for a global optimum (e.g., Huffman Encoding, Activity Scheduling).
- Graph Algorithms: Traversal, topological sorting, shortest paths (Warshall's and Floyd's algorithms), and Maximum Flow.
- Computability & Complexity: Introduction to P, NP, and NP-Complete problem classes.

## Exam Takeaways
- Algorithm Correctness: Be prepared to write loop invariants (Initialization, Maintenance, Termination) and use mathematical induction for recursive algorithms.
- Complexity Analysis: Know how to set up and solve recurrence relations and analyze worst, best, and average-case behaviors using the RAM Model.
- Dynamic Programming vs. Divide & Conquer: Understand when overlapping subproblems apply, requiring memoization or bottom-up tabulation.
- NP-Completeness: Recognize formal definitions and examples of NP-Complete problems for final exam conceptual questions.
